accepted_edits.reason: edits make exactly the five changes the answered findings promised: sbatch submission via a shared helper, --time HH:MM:SS assertion, log contract, followup wiring, section title

findings.reason: the plan would have a node implement a submission form the same repository already tested and rejected, sending every promotion's gate back onto the fleet node while the section claims it moved off it.
findings.text:
§19 tells the worker to submit the replayed command with `srun --partition=

--time= --chdir=` and states that clearing SLURM_JOB_ID and SLURM_JOBID makes it "a new job and not a step of the fleet allocation"; the cited precedent `landing_measure._partition_runner` (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:625-629) carries the recorded finding "srun from the fleet itself would stay inside the fleet allocation even when it names a different partition" and submits through `sbatch --wait` with `--nodes`, `--mem`, `--cpus-per-task` and every `SLURM_*`/`SBATCH_*` variable stripped, not just the two ids — so the chosen verb cannot deliver the section's own endpoint and would run the replay on the cores the section exists to protect

findings.reason: without an assertion on `--time` the node can deliver a run whose overrun safety silently fails by a factor of sixty, and the section's stated control that "the scheduler ends an overrun" is then untrue and untested.
findings.text: §19's done-when asserts only that the recorded argv starts with `srun` and names `--partition=all_debug` and `--chdir`, the environment, the long-partition case and the in-place fallback; nothing asserts the submitted `--time` value, though the deliverable's only guarantee that an abandoned job stops is "the job's `--time` equals the replay bound", and SLURM reads a bare integer `--time` as minutes, so a bound carried in seconds would give the job sixty times its bound and pass every stated assertion

findings.reason: a coordinator reading the plan has an invocation only for landed work and none for the one section a worker can build, so the new section cannot be dispatched without an out-of-band instruction and the two open followups would dispatch already-landed nodes.
findings.text: §19 is declared the plan's only implementable section but appears nowhere in the followups: f-aprteig-017 and f-aprteig-018 are open and name §17 and §18, both declared done, while no open followup carries `/reckon-build a-promotion-reads-the-evidence-it-is-given §19`

findings.reason: the dispatch manifest contract already requires the gate log path and a trailing exit line, so the omission changes no node's behaviour — but restoring the clause keeps §19 self-contained.
findings.text: §19 omits the clause every other section carries, that every log sits under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command and ends in `EXIT=`, so a node can satisfy the section with arm logs left wherever the test put them

findings.reason: the id is `s19` and the declarations key on it, so nothing else refers to the missing number; it is a display slip only.
findings.text: §19's heading reads "A gate replay runs on the measure partition, never on the fleet node" where every other section is titled "§<n> — …", so the section a followup must name by number is the one title that does not carry it

The done-when now asserts the submitted --time is the replay bound rendered as HH:MM:SS (a 450 s bound reads 00:07:30), and that the replay's stdout is read back from the job's log file.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `rerun_gate_at_integrated_revision` (reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:591), its single `subprocess.run` (:787), `replay_domain_invariant_checks` (:870), `landing_measure._partition_runner` (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:553), `measure_partition`/`measure_long_partition` (landing_measure.py:751,792; reckon/flight.py:1415) and the station caller (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:4064) all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §19's four assertions and its negative control read only the recorded argv, and none asserts the `--time` value the deliverable rests on to end an overrun (plan.html:138).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §19 is the only section that does not require its arm logs to sit under the run directory with a revision header and a trailing `EXIT=` line.
rubric_items.naming: a finding — §19's heading carries no section number, unlike every other section, so the plan's own `§19` references resolve to a title that does not name itself.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §19 prescribes `srun` and claims that removing SLURM_JOB_ID and SLURM_JOBID makes the replay "a new job and not a step of the fleet node's allocation", while the module it cites as its model records the opposite and submits with `sbatch` (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:625-629).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §19 names one deliverable, the replay executor's execution target, and its checks all measure that.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — no open followup names §19, the only implementable section, while f-aprteig-017 and f-aprteig-018 stay open for §17 and §18, which the declarations record as done (plan.html:21,178,183).
